title: Using AI to help create Stuffie Combat, my indie game
author: MikeFloorwalker
selftext:
I'm a solo developer. I have no coding background. I'm making a 2.5D fighting game with a 12-character roster, custom combat mechanics, and a full single-player mode. AI is writing the code. AI is helping generate art assets I'm not capable of producing myself.



Here's what I'm doing without AI: designing every character and combat system from scratch, sketching all character concepts by hand, composing and producing the entire soundtrack, handling all sound design.



I have complicated feelings about this. I'm aware of the conversation around AI and creative work, and I don't think it's a simple one. But the alternative to making this game with AI assistance isn't making it the traditional way. The alternative is not making it at all.



I'd rather make the game.



I'll talk openly about this as development continues... what's working, what isn't, where it gets weird. If you have strong opinions either way, I'm genuinely interested.

comments.author: N1t0_prime
comments.body: Learn to walk before you run.

replies.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
replies.body: Yeah I dunno that does seem pretty ambitious for a first project if it is your first project. I would do like a four character really simple art style thing first or something like that.

replies.author: MikeFloorwalker
replies.body: I understand! I’m know it’s kind of unhinged, and I should probably do what you suggested. But I don’t want to. I wanna make the whole damn game, and I learn fast.

comments.author: mallcopsarebastards
comments.body:
my honest opinion is if you don't want to put your project or your emotional well-being at risk, dont' talk about the dev process publicly. Some of the major studios are already pushing back against labeling requirements from distribution platforms like steam, because the stigma is so bad and the dog pilers are so radicalized.

I give it 6months before steam and other distributors completely drop their labeling requirements under high powered lobby pressure.

replies.author: re-skob
replies.body: I give it 6 months before it doesn't matter as everyone will be openly talking about it and it'll be known that most games are being made with some Gen AI

replies.author: mallcopsarebastards
replies.body: I think it's much more likely that nobody will be talking about it to the general audience the same way nobody is telling the general audience what game engine their using.

replies.author: MikeFloorwalker
replies.body: Interesting take. I feel better being open about it, but what you’re saying makes a lot of sense, no denying that.

comments.author: Crawling_Hustler
comments.body: There was a time when developer meant programmer. A programmer is a person who can code. Gone r those days

replies.author: MikeFloorwalker
replies.body: I honestly get what you’re saying. I’m in no way a programmer. I do intend to learn as much C Sharp as I can while I’m doing this.

comments.author: Ill-Past4609
comments.body: Have you found a nice setup for creating 2D animation yet ???

replies.author: MikeFloorwalker
replies.body: I’m gonna use a simple ComfyUI setup to help me do skeleton animations from sketches that I’ll create. I’ll give frame sets to my coding AI as reference once I have the art assets.

replies.author: Ill-Past4609
replies.body: Wow really how ? Using which Ai?
